draft_evidence.quote:
Thornwater's wall was timber on a stone footing, and the gate-walk ran along the inside of it at the height of a tall man's reach, and at dusk on the hundred and tenth day the bowman went off it to eat and left it to whoever wanted it, which was nobody, most evenings, and tonight was two.

He had had it since the stone and it had not grown, which he had noticed on the walk and filed as the only measurement of the thing he had: six weeks, and a fact that had not got one sentence longer for being carried.

comparison_evidence.quote:
## After Chapter 9 (CLOSED — PASS r2) — the stone at the line, Fallow Ring at dusk
- Timeline: Lowmarch left on the NINETY-FIRST day past the Line after the recovery slip was marked at the plank (HOLD, five names) in front of the meadow; Thornwater reached on the afternoon of the NINETY-THIRD; six leave Thornwater's east gate on the NINETY-FOURTH; the line at the Fallow road's second-day bend reached in the hour before dusk on the NINETY-FIFTH; camp that night on the road at the stone.

findings.consequence: From the stone on day 95 to the disclosure on day 110 is fifteen days, not six weeks. The error is repeated in Cael's spoken disclosure and closing log, making his central delay look nearly three times longer and materially changing the moral weight of how long he withheld the fact.
findings.repair_target: Reconcile every claimed duration of carrying the Ring fact with the day-95/day-110 calendar while preserving the fixed disclosure lines.

draft_evidence.quote: "The report's on a desk by now," Seln said. "The ferry went a fortnight ago. Whoever wrote the slip has read that we came out, and is deciding what that's worth."

comparison_evidence.quote:
## After Chapter 13 (CLOSED pending editor recheck r2 on one MEDIUM continuity repair; r1 PASS_WITH_FINDINGS) — Thornwater, the deep reading (~day 100)
- Timeline: the two-day walk from the stone (98th–99th) is summary; Chapter 13 opens at Thornwater's gate at the end of the NINETY-NINTH day

findings.consequence: A fortnight before the manuscript's day 110 is day 96, but the crew did not return to Thornwater until day 99; a completed report saying they came out could not have left on that ferry. The line installs an impossible ordinary transmission path immediately before the packet's deliberately unexplained misrouting plant.
findings.repair_target: Remove or reconcile the ferry-based timing explanation so the required report can reach Vastin through the packet's anomalous, unexplained route without departing before completion existed.

draft_evidence.quote: "Oxhollow's eleven days late and the old woman's knee doesn't care what's under a floor. I'll be on the road at first light and I'll be three days north by the time you're back at the board."

comparison_evidence.quote: She had said so at the bend, and she said it again on the hundred and fourth day, at the house door, to the woman, in the voice for a distance: "I'm nine days late here and eleven at the next. Send me who's hurt."

findings.consequence: The next stop is already eleven days late on day 104; Chapter 16 is explicitly day 110, so the delay should have accrued another six days. Repeating eleven also in the final log freezes the arithmetic of Oryn's independent route precisely when that cost drives her departure and will govern her Chapter 17 position.
findings.repair_target: Reconcile the current Oxhollow/route lateness with six further days at Thornwater while retaining the required intention to leave north at first light.

draft_evidence.quote: Vastin received the broker's completion report as a courtesy copy, forwarded through a provincial registry office that had no interest in any board east of the Line, in the second folder of the morning, marked *Fallow Ring: crew returned, instruments not recovered*. He read it twice — a broker's report from a town on no registry map, on his desk with no routing note and no requesting officer's name — and did not know why it had reached him, and filed that, in the register of a man who had never once in forty years pretended to knowledge he lacked, as the whole of what he knew about it. He returned the copy to its folder unannotated.

findings.consequence: Calling the forwarding office provincial and specifying that no requesting officer is named adds two routing facts without an approved exception. The window is designed to plant unexplained arrival while tightly withholding how the report moved; these details silently narrow that future explanation.
findings.repair_target: Keep the required uninterested registry office and absent routing note, but remove unapproved routing specifics or obtain an explicit approval record.

strengths: Yes: worldbuilding is done through mechanism and use. The gate-walk shows how Thornwater closes; the board and map turn work into a search method; Oryn's delay accumulates as route debt; the report climbs through forms and folders; and the new power's moral law becomes an actual consent procedure entered in the log.

There is no present fight, exactly as prohibited. The noncombat set pieces are memorably choreographed and their terrain is load-bearing: the wall lets Lira and Cael face the road instead of each other, the six fixed seats turn the common-room table into an evidence circle, and the well isolates the consent covenant. Its win-sentence is writable: Oryn removes Cael's ability to mistake unnoticed contact-reading for harmless curiosity by binding it to an ask-first rule he must reread with every inventory.

The Lira scene pays six books of trust without turning into a declaration of affection. Her answer restores the original covenant, her fighter's follow-up tests cost rather than ontology, and the good hand against his boot supplies earned contact without explaining it.

The circle differentiates all six by competence. Brom reports weight and cost, Karis controls the evidentiary sequence, Seln supplies the institutional clock, Oryn limits her claim clinically, and Lira confirms from closest range; unanimity emerges through six methods rather than six matching speeches.

The temptation is concrete and morally losable. A wrist one foot from Cael's hand gives the risk a repeatable physical trigger, while 'the days I don't notice I've started' makes the rule protect against habit rather than melodramatic intent.

The required ending lands as changed pressure. It joins the freedom pole, the exception at the line, Karis's restraint, the new search, and Pike's warning in one audible log entry, and it differs cleanly from Chapter 15's dialogue close.

Production discipline is strong: 4,664 words is within tolerance; section 8.4 metadata, section 10 summary, modern-register, feeling/growth, pitch, and chapter-level tic searches are clean; attribution survives the six-speaker scene; names pass the registry ear check; and injury/fragment state is carried accurately.
concerns: Taste only: the five closing log paragraphs repeat nearly every emotional and strategic result immediately after the wall, table, and well have dramatized it. The fixed final paragraph is strong; a later compression pass could test how much preceding recap it needs to retain maximum force.

Taste only: Brom's ladder speech is affecting and voice-specific, but its claim that Cael was 'the only one who worked' in every major room risks generalizing the Ring's distinctive terror into a familiar pattern. A human may prefer either the comfort of that continuity or the sharper singularity of the Quieting.

Taste only: Oryn's repeat-reading condition productively protects Chapter 22 and fits her method, but it adds a second rule immediately after the ask-first covenant. The scene remains clear; audio performance should preserve which rule governs consent and which governs confidence in Cael's self-reading.
